target_customer: Urban lunch and dinner customers in Berkeley, Emeryville and San Francisco wanting cheap fast meals
problem: Quality prepared meals were slow or expensive to get. SpoonRocket cooked meals centrally and delivered them in about ten minutes for a few dollars.
business_model: Vertically integrated meal delivery at a flat low price per meal with no delivery fee

founders.name: Steven Hsiao
education: UC Berkeley (graduate, per California magazine snippet)

founders.name: Anson Tsui
education: UC Berkeley (graduate, per California magazine snippet)

exit.reason: Told investors it was shutting down after failing to raise the capital needed to continue; iFood later acquired the technology.

competitors.name: Sprig
competitors.what: Fresh organic meals delivered in about 15 minutes

technical_complexity.rationale: Routing and batching software plus heated delivery vehicles, but the hard part was operations and logistics rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Central kitchen and delivery operations were copyable and capital hungry; several rivals launched at the same time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals and later UberEats entered the same market; SpoonRocket shut in March 2016 and Sprig followed in 2017.

market_need_then: Time poor urban customers wanted fast, cheap meals; early coverage cited growth in on-demand delivery. The model of owning food production and delivery at $8 or less per meal proved hard to fund.

branding.domain_note: Used spoonrocket.com; it no longer resolves from this environment.

rebrands.why: Shifted from late night student delivery to a broader, more health conscious customer base per California magazine snippet

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage as part of the on-demand wave; no fan community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name tied to a clear promise and wide press, but short lived and no evidence the brand drove growth.

pivots.from: Late Night Option, late night food delivery for Berkeley students
pivots.to: SpoonRocket, meals for a broader older customer base
pivots.why: Targeted a more health conscious customer

outcome_analysis: SpoonRocket raised about 13.5M including an 11M Series A in 2014 and expanded from Berkeley to San Francisco with a low priced vertically integrated meal model. It faced intense competition from Sprig and others in a tightening funding environment and failed to raise the next round, shutting down in March 2016. Its technology was later bought by iFood, so the directory label Acquired reflects an asset sale, not a company exit.
notes: Directory status says Acquired, but sources report shutdown in March 2016 with iFood buying the technology. Competitors are from a May 2014 article, the closest dated source to the batch. Fortune snippet says Foundation led the Series A, FinSMEs says General Catalyst participated; lead conflicts across outlets. Seed amount of 2.5M and total of 13.5M come from a search snippet of Fortune and are only partly verified. spoonrocket.com failed DNS resolution, possibly a network limit; not worked around.
